name: MathlibAnnex.FiniteRecovery.nonempty_almostIsometryMatch_of_all_body_eq
title: Equal Plücker bodies yield matching generators with an almost-isometric representative

content.display_title: Equal Plücker bodies yield matching generators with an almost-isometric representative
content.one_sentence_role: Selects common minor coordinates with a target almost-isometric representative.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n=m+1>0$ and $V=\mathbb R^n$ with the reference sup norm and standard Lebesgue measure $\lambda$. The continuous norms $p,q$ have fixed positive comparison constants
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty,\qquad
a_q\|x\|_\infty\le q(x)\le b_q\|x\|_\infty.$$
Set $K_p=\{x:p(x)\le1\}$, $K_q=\{x:q(x)\le1\}$ and $v_p=\lambda(K_p)$, $v_q=\lambda(K_q)$, as positive finite real numbers. For a real linear map $A:V\to\mathbb R^N$, let $A_{ij}=(Ae_j)_i$ be its matrix in the standard bases. The minor-coordinate space has one coordinate for each increasing $n$-tuple $I$ of distinct rows from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and
$$\Pi_n(A)_I=\det(A_{I,*}).$$
Define the signed generator set and its real convex hull by
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal G_p^N
 &=\left\{\sigma v_p\Pi_n(A):\begin{array}{l}
       A:V\to\mathbb R^N\text{ is real linear},\ \sigma\in\{1,-1\},\\
       \|Ax\|_\infty\le p(x)\quad(x\in V)
       \end{array}\right\},\\
\mathcal P_p^N&=\operatorname{conv}_{\mathbb R}\mathcal G_p^N.
\end{aligned}$$
Define $\mathcal G_q^N,\mathcal P_q^N$ in the same way using $q,v_q$. The generators are vectors of minors, not linear maps. Suppose $\varepsilon>0$ and $\mathcal P_p^N=\mathcal P_q^N$ for every $N$. There exist a dimension $N$, one minor vector $z$, and real linear maps $B_p,B_q:V\to\mathbb R^N$ with
$$\forall x,\ \|B_px\|_\infty\le p(x),\qquad
\forall x,\ \|B_qx\|_\infty\le q(x),$$
$$\forall x\ (q(x)=1),\quad 1-\varepsilon<\|B_qx\|_\infty,$$
$$z=\sigma_pv_p\Pi_n(B_p)=\sigma_qv_q\Pi_n(B_q),\qquad
\sigma_p,\sigma_q\in\{1,-1\}.$$
content.assumptions: The two norm models, $\varepsilon>0$, and body equality for every finite target dimension are inputs. No upper restriction on $\varepsilon$ is required.
content.conclusion: One dimension and one raw minor vector are shared. Both maps are contractive, but only $B_q$ is required to have the almost lower condition. The signs need not coincide.
content.proof_summary: Choose target satellite parameters, refine the same support on the two compact raw sets, then extract the two representatives.

proof_steps.text: **Choose parameters for the target norm.** Let $D_q>0$ be the maximum absolute determinant of $q$-dominated base rows; its positivity is [the determinant-maximum lemma](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/FiniteRecovery.lean#L69-L70). Put $\eta=D_q/2$. Then $0<\eta<D_q$. Apply [the target satellite package](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L1115-L1134) with $q,\eta,\varepsilon$. It supplies $K>0$, radius $\min(\varepsilon,1)/(8K)$, net $C_{\mathrm{net}}$ and $w>0$ with strict satellite budget $<w\eta$. Fix $N=n+|C_{\mathrm{net}}|$ and the oriented linear support $\ell$ of its selected absolute maximizer.

**Choose a common raw point in this support direction.** For the selected linear functional $\ell$, set
$$\mathcal F_q=\{z\in\mathcal G_q^N:
              \ell(z)=\max_{u\in\mathcal G_q^N}\ell(u)\}.$$
The [raw-slice theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/FiniteRecovery.lean#L517-L551) applied to the target parameters says that every $z\in\mathcal F_q$ has a real linear representative $B_q$ such that
$$\begin{gathered}
\|B_qx\|_\infty\le q(x)\quad(x\in V),\\
1-\varepsilon<\|B_qx\|_\infty\quad(q(x)=1),\qquad
z=\pm v_q\Pi_n(B_q).
\end{gathered}$$
The two raw sets $\mathcal G_p^N,\mathcal G_q^N$ are [compact](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Convex/PluckerBody.lean#L67-L90) and [nonempty](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Convex/PluckerBody.lean#L30-L32) and have equal convex hulls by the input at this $N$. Apply [common raw selection](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Convex/LexicographicSelection.lean#L362-L372) to these sets, this same $\ell$, and the displayed property of every point in its target maximum slice. It returns
$$z\in\mathcal G_p^N\cap\mathcal G_q^N$$
with the displayed target-representative properties. This selects a particular common raw point; it does not infer that the two raw sets are equal.

**Extract two representatives of the same point.** Source raw membership gives $B_p$, its contractivity and $z=\sigma_pv_p\Pi_n(B_p)$. Target goodness gives $B_q$, contractivity, lower condition and $z=\sigma_qv_q\Pi_n(B_q)$. Thus
$$\sigma_pv_p\Pi_n(B_p)=z=\sigma_qv_q\Pi_n(B_q).$$
The [fixed-dimension construction](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/FiniteRecovery.lean#L602-L629) places these same maps in all nine fields, retaining the separate signs.

content.lean_realization_notes: The lower condition is required only for the target representative $B_q$. No lower estimate for $B_p$ or square factorization map is asserted at this stage.
